title: Smallest unsatisfiable subsets
description: Sets of at most k clauses of a formula that are unsatisfiable together; existence is Sigma-2-complete (Liberatore). The check finds an assignment that satisfies the picked clauses, and the refinement says that a clause it falsifies has to be picked, so the abstraction collects hitting-set constraints. With k = 4 the two smallest cores come out; try k = 5 (23 solutions).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The formula, as facts. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
clause(C) :- pos(C,_).
clause(C) :- neg(C,_).
var(V) :- pos(_,V).
var(V) :- neg(_,V).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): sets of at most k clauses.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k clauses of the formula.
{ pick(C) : clause(C) } k.
#show pick/1.
% 'always' is true in every candidate. The check blames it when a counterexample does
% not depend on the candidate: then no candidate is a solution, and the clause "always
% must change" ends the search.
{ always }.
:- not always.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the picked clauses.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for an assignment that satisfies the picked clauses (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: an assignment that satisfies every picked clause.
{ t(V) } :- var(V).
sat(C) :- pos(C,V), t(V).
sat(C) :- neg(C,V), not t(V).
:- pick(C), not sat(C).
#show t/1.

% The assignment satisfies every set of clauses that avoids the clauses it falsifies.
% So one of those has to be picked: a positive clause over atoms that are false now.
relevant(pick(C)) :- clause(C), not sat(C).
% An assignment that satisfies the whole formula falsifies none: the formula is then
% satisfiable and has no unsatisfiable subset. Blame the atom that is always true.
falsified :- clause(C), not sat(C).
relevant(always) :- not falsified.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% An unsatisfiable formula in conjunctive normal form over v1..v5.
% pos(C,V): clause C contains variable V, neg(C,V): its negation.
neg(1,1).                             % ~v1
pos(2,1). neg(2,2).                   % v1 | ~v2
neg(3,2). neg(3,4).                   % ~v2 | ~v4
pos(4,2). neg(4,3).                   % v2 | ~v3
pos(5,2). pos(5,3).                   % v2 | v3
pos(6,2). neg(6,4).                   % v2 | ~v4
neg(7,3). pos(7,5).                   % ~v3 | v5
pos(8,3). neg(8,4).                   % v3 | ~v4
pos(9,3). pos(9,4).                   % v3 | v4
pos(10,3). pos(10,5).                 % v3 | v5
pos(11,1). pos(11,2). pos(11,4).      % v1 | v2 | v4
pos(12,1). pos(12,3). pos(12,4).      % v1 | v3 | v4

% The formula of example with k = 5: every unsatisfiable set of at most 5 of its clauses.
neg(1,1).                             % ~v1
pos(2,1). neg(2,2).                   % v1 | ~v2
neg(3,2). neg(3,4).                   % ~v2 | ~v4
pos(4,2). neg(4,3).                   % v2 | ~v3
pos(5,2). pos(5,3).                   % v2 | v3
pos(6,2). neg(6,4).                   % v2 | ~v4
neg(7,3). pos(7,5).                   % ~v3 | v5
pos(8,3). neg(8,4).                   % v3 | ~v4
pos(9,3). pos(9,4).                   % v3 | v4
pos(10,3). pos(10,5).                 % v3 | v5
pos(11,1). pos(11,2). pos(11,4).      % v1 | v2 | v4
pos(12,1). pos(12,3). pos(12,4).      % v1 | v3 | v4

% A satisfiable formula: it has no unsatisfiable subset at all.
pos(1,1). pos(1,2).                   % v1 | v2
neg(2,1). pos(2,3).                   % ~v1 | v3
neg(3,2). neg(3,3).                   % ~v2 | ~v3

% Two chains of implications from v1 to ~v1: v1, v1 -> v2 -> ~v1 and v1 -> v3 -> v4 -> ~v1.
pos(1,1).                             % v1
neg(2,1). pos(2,2).                   % ~v1 | v2
neg(3,2). neg(3,1).                   % ~v2 | ~v1
neg(4,1). pos(4,3).                   % ~v1 | v3
neg(5,3). pos(5,4).                   % ~v3 | v4
neg(6,4). neg(6,1).                   % ~v4 | ~v1
pos(7,2). pos(7,4).                   % v2 | v4

generators.name: random-cnf
generators.description: A random CNF: c clauses over the variables 1..v, each with 1 to l literals.
generators.text:
% random-cnf: c clauses over the variables 1..v; clause C has 1 to l literals (uniform), each
% on a uniform variable with a sign of probability 1/2 (a repeated literal counts once).
clause(1..c).
len(C,@int(1, l, C, len)) :- clause(C).
lit(C,J,@int(1, v, C, J)) :- len(C,N), J = 1..N.
pos(C,V) :- lit(C,J,V), @flip(500, C, J, sign) = 1.
neg(C,V) :- lit(C,J,V), @flip(500, C, J, sign) = 0.
#show pos/2.
#show neg/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three satisfying assignments per candidate, one clause each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

spaces.name: formulas
spaces.description: Every CNF with size non-empty clauses over size variables; MUSes of at most k clauses.
spaces.text:
% every CNF with the clauses 1..size over the variables 1..size; no clause is empty
cid(1..size).  vid(1..size).
{ pos(C,V) : cid(C), vid(V) }.
{ neg(C,V) : cid(C), vid(V) }.
:- cid(C), not pos(C,_), not neg(C,_).
